name: Unakoti Heritage Site (Rock Carvings)
description: Ancient open-air gallery of colossal rock-cut sculptures and bas-reliefs of Hindu deities, primarily Shaivite, carved into the hillsides of Unakoti. Centerpiece is the ~30-foot Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava (Shiva head). Dates to 7th-9th century CE; UNESCO Tentative World Heritage Site since 2022. Also known as Subrai Khung.
facts: Name means 'one less than a crore' from local legend of 99,99,999 carvings
About 8 km east of Kailashahar, 178 km from Agartala
Annual Ashokastami Mela attracts thousands of pilgrims
ASI protected site with streams and forested setting

name: Jampui Hills
description: Highest hill range in Tripura (~3,000 ft), known as the Eternal Hills of Spring or Orchid Paradise of India. Features lush greenery, orange orchards, misty landscapes, and panoramic views toward Mizoram and Bangladesh.
facts: Average elevation around 1,000 m; highest peak Betlingchhip at 930 m.
About 200-220 km from Agartala; nearest railhead Dharmanagar (~70 km).
Home to over 50 orchid species including rare Vanda coerulea.
Eden Tourist Lodge and local paying guest stays in Vanghmun.

name: Betlingchhip Peak
description: Highest point in Tripura at 930 m (also called Thaidawr or Betalongchhip), located on the Jampui ridge. Offers sunrise views of stacked ridges toward Mizoram hills and Bangladesh plains.
facts: Elevation 930 m, highest in the state.
Short walk or scramble from the road near Vanghmun.
Best at sunrise before mist fills the valleys.
Part of Jampui Hills range bordering Mizoram.

name: Vanghmun Village
description: Cleanest village in Tripura, perched on the Jampui ridge. Features neat Mizo homes, orange orchards, church, and access to viewpoints and homestays for authentic hill culture.
facts: Headquarters of Jampui Hills block; police station present.
Known for community cleanliness efforts.
Eden Tourist Lodge and local paying guests available.
About 220 km from Agartala, 55 km from Aizawl.

name: Rowa Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Compact wildlife sanctuary near Panisagar (about 86 hectares), rich in birds, primates, reptiles, and mixed forests. Ideal for short eco-trails, birdwatching, and peaceful nature visits.
facts: Established 1988; only sanctuary in northern Tripura.
About 18 km from Dharmanagar, 4-5 km from Panisagar.
Home to over 60 bird species, langurs, deer, and reptiles.
No permit required; accessible trails.

name: Shilchhara Buddha Waterfall
description: Hidden gem waterfall near Pecharthal, cascading amid lush forest with a Buddha statue beside the falls. Offers serene walks, meditation spots, and quiet immersion in nature.
facts: Located near Pecharthal in North Tripura.
Features a Buddha idol by the falls for peaceful ambiance.
Accessible via forest trails; best in non-monsoon for safety.
Lesser-known alternative to more crowded sites.

name: Kalibari Temple (Dharmanagar)
description: Prominent Kali temple in Dharmanagar town, serving as a spiritual and cultural center for local devotees. Active during festivals like Kali Puja with community gatherings.
facts: Located in Dharmanagar, headquarters of North Tripura.
Focal point for religious festivals and local culture.
Simple traditional architecture in a serene setting.
Accessible within the town.

name: Dharmanagar
description: Headquarters and largest town of North Tripura district, near the Bangladesh border. Gateway to Jampui Hills, Rowa Sanctuary, and other northern attractions, with markets and rail connectivity.
facts: Administrative center of North Tripura.
Nearest major railhead for Jampui Hills (~70 km).
Juri River flows through the town.
About 180-200 km from Agartala.
